Viavi Exhibits More Than Threefold Growth in a Year: Should You Buy?
Viavi Solutions Inc. VIAV has surged 268.5% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 148.5%. It has outperformed peers like Corning Incorporated GLW and Ooma, Inc. OOMA. While Corning has gained 92.4%, OOMA jumped 79.9% during this period. The more than threefold growth was largely buoyed by growing investor optimism over Viavi's rising exposure to artificial intelligence (AI)-driven data-center spending, improving profitability and expanding testing capabilities.
AI Data-Center Boom: Key Growth Catalyst
Viavi is increasingly benefiting from the rapid buildout of AI and hyperscale data center infrastructure. Demand for high-speed optical, Ethernet and network-testing solutions remains healthy as cloud service providers, semiconductor companies and networking vendors invest heavily in increasingly complex AI infrastructure.
The data-center ecosystem now accounts for roughly half of Network and Service Enablement (NSE) revenues, underscoring the growing importance of this market to Viavi's growth profile.
In the fiscal fourth quarter, NSE revenues surged 69.2% year over year to $353.9 million.
Growth was supported by robust demand for lab, production and field-testing solutions, strength in aerospace and defense and contributions from the acquired Spirent businesses. The Spirent assets have also strengthened Viavi's capabilities in high-speed Ethernet testing, network security and channel emulation. The broader portfolio should support cross-selling opportunities while helping the company address increasingly sophisticated testing requirements across AI clusters and next-generation networks.
Margin Expansion Strengthens the Earnings Story
Viavi exited fiscal 2026 on a strong note, with both revenues and profitability exhibiting healthy improvement. Revenues increased 40% year over year to $1.52 billion, while non-GAAP earnings surged 112.8% to $1 per share.
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 630 basis points to 20.6%. The sharp improvement highlights stronger operating leverage and suggests that rising revenues are translating effectively into earnings growth.
This margin expansion is particularly encouraging as Viavi integrates Spirent and increases its exposure to higher-growth markets such as AI data centers, aerospace and defense and advanced wireless testing.
Upbeat Outlook Points to Continued Momentum
Management expects the positive momentum to extend into fiscal 2027. For the fiscal first quarter, Viavi projects revenues in the range of $450 million to $460 million and non-GAAP earnings of 40-42 cents per share. Both metrics indicate sequential improvement from the June quarter.
The outlook suggests that healthy demand trends are continuing across several important end markets. In addition to AI-related data-center opportunities, aerospace and defense remain a key growth avenue, particularly for positioning, navigation and timing solutions. Strength in these markets also helps diversify Viavi's business and reduces its historical dependence on telecom carrier spending.
6G and Wireless Testing: Other Growth Pillars
Viavi is also positioning itself for emerging opportunities in next-generation wireless technologies. The company's Vertex 6.0 advanced channel emulator is designed for 6G and Wi-Fi 7/8 testing. The platform supports up to 400 MHz of instantaneous bandwidth and carrier frequencies of up to 23.6 GHz, while extending across cellular, Wi-Fi, military and aerospace applications.
Viavi is also participating in the SHIELD-6G project, using its TeraVM AI RAN Scenario Generator to develop digital twins for AI-driven security testing. These developments broaden Viavi's wireless-testing opportunity and provide exposure to emerging markets such as 6G, Wi-Fi, AI-RAN and specialized RF testing. Although these markets are still developing, early positioning could give VIAVI additional long-term growth opportunities.
The earnings estimate trend also remains favorable. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Viavi's fiscal 2027 earnings has increased 165.6% over the past year to $1.62 per share. Upward earnings estimate revisions generally reflect improving confidence in a company's operating outlook. In Viavi's case, the positive trend appears consistent with improving margins, healthy demand and growing contributions from acquired businesses.
Should Investors Chase Viavi After the Rally?
Viavi's 268.5% share price rally has been supported by a substantial improvement in business fundamentals. AI data-center demand is strengthening, the Spirent acquisition has expanded the company's addressable market, profitability is improving and aerospace and defense continue to provide diversification. The company also appears well-positioned to benefit from long-term growth opportunities in 6G, Wi-Fi, AI-RAN and advanced network testing.

CHANDLER, Ariz., Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- VIAVI Solutions Inc. (VIAVI) (NASDAQ: VIAV) today introduced the CyberFlood CF50, the industry's smallest and lightest all-in-one platform for enterprise-scale application performance, security, AI inference and large-language model (LLM) testing up to 100G.
CyberFlood CF50 also features the industry’s lowest power consumption and highest TLS performance with native PQC support
Increasingly encrypted applications, Zero Trust architectures and AI-driven services require validation to go beyond infrastructure capacity and examine the impact of security controls and network performance on application responsiveness and user experience. The CF50 generates highly realistic encrypted and mixed application traffic to help organizations assess performance, scalability, resilience and quality of experience before deployment.
The highly portable and power-efficient 1U appliance combines realistic Layer 4-7 traffic generation, security assessment and AI inference testing capabilities in a cost-effective platform, bringing enterprise-scale testing to a wide range of network equipment manufacturers, systems integrators and service providers. It offers the industry's lowest power consumption, as well as native PQC support and a TLS performance that is 1.75X that of the nearest competitor.
The CF50 includes an easy-to-use web interface for the validation of modern network and security infrastructure. It has no requirement for an MS Windows client and includes the ability to implement automated goal-seeking, MITRE ATT&CK frameworks and repeatable traffic-mix testing.
"As organizations deploy increasingly complex combinations of AI workloads, encrypted applications and distributed security architectures, the ability to validate performance under realistic conditions is becoming a critical requirement rather than an optional capability," said Mauricio Sanchez, Senior Director, Enterprise Security and Networking, Dell'Oro Group. "Organizations need testing solutions that can accurately emulate real-world users, applications and AI interactions to help identify bottlenecks, optimize infrastructure investments and reduce deployment risk."
"The CyberFlood CF50 combines realistic application traffic, security validation and AI inference testing in a highly portable platform, enabling customers to validate infrastructure at scale, accelerate deployment decisions and improve confidence in production readiness," said Sashi Jeyaretnam, Senior Director, Security Product Management, VIAVI. "It provides a practical way for organizations to validate performance before complex AI-enabled and security-driven services go live."
The CF50 joins the CyberFlood CF1000, which is targeted at large enterprises demanding the highest level of performance.

VIAV's NSE Segment Shows Strength: Is the Growth Story Intact?
VIAVI Solutions Inc. VIAV is seeing strong momentum in its Network and Service Enablement (NSE) business. During the fourth quarter, NSE's Segment revenues reached $353.9 million, up 69.2% year over year, exceeding the company's guidance range of $340-$348 million. There are several factors driving this uptick.
The data center ecosystem is now a contributor to VIAVI's NSE business growth. The company is witnessing demand from semiconductor companies, optical module manufacturers, network equipment manufacturers and hyperscalers. Companies in this sector are rapidly adopting testing solutions across research and development, production, deployment, maintenance and network monitoring. Migration toward higher-speed networking is another major contributor. 800G remains the largest volume driver currently. The ramp of 1.6-terabit technology is expected to be another growth driver in upcoming quarters.
The integration of selected Spirent product lines is another tailwind for NSE. The acquisition strengthens VIAVI's portfolio in high-speed Ethernet and expands its capabilities in network validation and security testing. VIAVI is also developing products for next-generation AI networks. In June 2026, the company introduced an Ultra Ethernet Transport validation solution for AI fabrics. The platform is designed for hyperscalers, cloud providers, neocloud operators and network equipment manufacturers. Such leading-edge innovation expands Viavi's addressable market beyond conventional telecom testing.
Management expects another strong performance in the first quarter of 2027 in the NSE segment. It expects NSE revenues of $360-$368 million compared with $353.9 million in the fiscal fourth quarter. NSE operating margin is expected at 23.1%, plus or minus 50 basis points.
Despite strong growth prospects, investors should also consider certain risk factors. Traditional wireless testing demand remains soft. Heavy reliance on continued data center investment and potential fluctuations in customer spending can create volatility in the NSE segment.
How Are Key Test-and-Measurement Peers Faring?
Keysight Technologies' KEYS CSG generated $1.35 billion in revenues, up from the year-ago quarter's $940 million. The 43% year-over-year increase was driven by strong performance in wireline and wireless, as well as continued momentum in AI infrastructure and aerospace, defense and government. Emerging 6G and non-terrestrial network opportunities also supported demand. Keysight's portfolio across design, emulation and test positions it to capture ongoing wireless and network investment cycles. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, wireless orders grew again as customers increased spending on next-generation connectivity and the supply chain supporting AI infrastructure.
Teradyne, Inc. TER is a provider of automated test equipment and robotics, with its operations spanning Semiconductor Test, Product Test and Robotics. Its testing portfolio covers semiconductors, wireless products, silicon photonics and complex electronics. Teradyne is also benefiting from the rise in AI-related semiconductor demand. In the second quarter of 2026, revenues reached a record $1.33 billion, up 104% year over year, with Semiconductor Test contributing $1.12 billion, Product Test $107 million and Robotics $100 million.
VIAV's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates
Viavi has gained 196% in the past year compared with the Electronics - Measuring Instruments industry's growth of 146.9%.
Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 22.82 forward earnings, lower than 35.95 for the industry and lower than its mean of 39.43.
The company's earnings estimates for 2026 and 2027 have improved over the past 60 days.

VIAVI Successfully Achieves CMMC Level 2 Certification
Certification to CMMC advanced cybersecurity standard strengthens company's position as a trusted partner to government, defense and national security partners
CHANDLER, Ariz., Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- VIAVI Solutions LLC, the Aerospace and Defense division of VIAVI Solutions Inc. (VIAVI) (NASDAQ: VIAV) today announced the successful completion of its Level 2 CMMC certification for its radio test, avionics, synthetic and modular, and Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) product lines.
Certification to CMMC advanced cybersecurity standard strengthens company’s position as a trusted partner to government, defense and national security partners
The CMMC assessment process was conducted by leading C3PAO A-LIGN, an experienced federal assessor and compliance partner trusted by more than 6,400 global organizations to help mitigate cybersecurity risks.
"Achieving CMMC Level 2 certification reflects our dedication to safeguarding the sensitive information that underpins national security and reinforces our role as a trusted partner to the U.S. Defense Industrial Base (DIB)," said Doug Russell, Senior Vice President and General Manager, Aerospace and Defense, VIAVI. "We look forward to extending the certification to the Inertial Labs product lines, which were acquired by VIAVI in 2025."
CMMC was developed by the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) to ensure that cybersecurity controls and processes adequately protect Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) that resides on DIB systems and networks to protect national security. This certification is mandatory for all entities doing business with the DoD.
"Congratulations to the VIAVI Aerospace and Defense team for achieving CMMC Level 2 certification. This accomplishment demonstrates a strong commitment to safeguarding valuable information to protect our nation, developing a competitive advantage, and creating a culture of security," said Petar Besalev, Executive Vice President of Compliance and Cybersecurity Services, A-LIGN. "We're proud to support this integral step in VIAVI's compliance journey with a high-quality assessment process and deep expertise in federal compliance."
This certification demonstrates VIAVI's commitment to safeguarding the United States' national security by complying with CMMC's rigorous standards and protecting federal contract information and CUI.
VIAVI (NASDAQ: VIAV) is a global leader in test and measurement and optical technologies. Our test and measurement, and resilient Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) solutions enable and secure critical infrastructure ranging from data center ecosystems and communication networks to military, aerospace, railway and first responder communications. In addition, we develop and advance technologies used in high-volume optical applications across anti-counterfeiting, consumer electronics, aerospace, industrial and automotive end markets.

What Happened?
A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after Treasury yields eased and crude oil prices fell amid U.S. and Iranian talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. stocks opened higher on Friday, with technology and industrials leading the advance, according to Industrial Info.
The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow waterway between Iran and Oman and a key route for global oil shipments, so any sign it could reopen tends to push crude prices down. Lower oil prices matter for industrial companies because fuel and energy are major costs for manufacturers, airlines, freight carriers and equipment makers. Cheaper energy can ease pressure on profit margins. Falling Treasury yields, which are the interest rates the U.S. government pays to borrow, also help. They tend to reduce borrowing costs across the economy, which can support spending on factories, machinery and infrastructure, areas where industrial firms earn much of their revenue.
Separately, Industrial Info Resources reported that the U.S. heavy-manufacturing industry is scheduled to start more than $12 billion in construction projects during the fourth quarter. It said the activity is driven by battery-storage systems and space exploration. The outlook remains tied to the U.S.-Iran discussions. Any setback in the talks could reverse the drop in oil prices and weigh on the sector again.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

U.S. stocks fell early Thursday, according to the Associated Press, as surging Treasury yields and rebounding energy prices weighed on financial markets. A Treasury yield is the return investors earn for lending money to the U.S. government. The 10-year yield is closely watched because it serves as a benchmark for many other borrowing costs, including mortgages and corporate loans. When it rises, it becomes more expensive for households and businesses to borrow, which can slow spending and investment. Higher yields can also make stocks look less attractive. When investors can earn a relatively safe return of more than 5% from government bonds, some may choose to move money out of riskier assets such as equities.
Companies that depend on borrowing to fund growth, or whose value is based heavily on expected future profits, often feel this pressure most. Rebounding energy prices added to the strain. Higher fuel costs can raise expenses for businesses and consumers and may keep inflation elevated, which could keep upward pressure on interest rates.
Taken together, the jump in yields to their highest level in roughly two decades and the rise in energy prices created a difficult backdrop for stocks across the sector, with many companies moving lower together.

Viavi Exhibits More Than Threefold Growth in a Year: Should You Buy?
Viavi Solutions Inc. VIAV has surged 268.5% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 148.5%. It has outperformed peers like Corning Incorporated GLW and Ooma, Inc. OOMA. While Corning has gained 92.4%, OOMA jumped 79.9% during this period. The more than threefold growth was largely buoyed by growing investor optimism over Viavi's rising exposure to artificial intelligence (AI)-driven data-center spending, improving profitability and expanding testing capabilities.
AI Data-Center Boom: Key Growth Catalyst
Viavi is increasingly benefiting from the rapid buildout of AI and hyperscale data center infrastructure. Demand for high-speed optical, Ethernet and network-testing solutions remains healthy as cloud service providers, semiconductor companies and networking vendors invest heavily in increasingly complex AI infrastructure.
The data-center ecosystem now accounts for roughly half of Network and Service Enablement (NSE) revenues, underscoring the growing importance of this market to Viavi's growth profile.
In the fiscal fourth quarter, NSE revenues surged 69.2% year over year to $353.9 million.
Growth was supported by robust demand for lab, production and field-testing solutions, strength in aerospace and defense and contributions from the acquired Spirent businesses. The Spirent assets have also strengthened Viavi's capabilities in high-speed Ethernet testing, network security and channel emulation. The broader portfolio should support cross-selling opportunities while helping the company address increasingly sophisticated testing requirements across AI clusters and next-generation networks.
Margin Expansion Strengthens the Earnings Story
Viavi exited fiscal 2026 on a strong note, with both revenues and profitability exhibiting healthy improvement. Revenues increased 40% year over year to $1.52 billion, while non-GAAP earnings surged 112.8% to $1 per share.
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 630 basis points to 20.6%. The sharp improvement highlights stronger operating leverage and suggests that rising revenues are translating effectively into earnings growth.
This margin expansion is particularly encouraging as Viavi integrates Spirent and increases its exposure to higher-growth markets such as AI data centers, aerospace and defense and advanced wireless testing.
Upbeat Outlook Points to Continued Momentum
Management expects the positive momentum to extend into fiscal 2027. For the fiscal first quarter, Viavi projects revenues in the range of $450 million to $460 million and non-GAAP earnings of 40-42 cents per share. Both metrics indicate sequential improvement from the June quarter.
The outlook suggests that healthy demand trends are continuing across several important end markets. In addition to AI-related data-center opportunities, aerospace and defense remain a key growth avenue, particularly for positioning, navigation and timing solutions. Strength in these markets also helps diversify Viavi's business and reduces its historical dependence on telecom carrier spending.
6G and Wireless Testing: Other Growth Pillars
Viavi is also positioning itself for emerging opportunities in next-generation wireless technologies. The company's Vertex 6.0 advanced channel emulator is designed for 6G and Wi-Fi 7/8 testing. The platform supports up to 400 MHz of instantaneous bandwidth and carrier frequencies of up to 23.6 GHz, while extending across cellular, Wi-Fi, military and aerospace applications.
Viavi is also participating in the SHIELD-6G project, using its TeraVM AI RAN Scenario Generator to develop digital twins for AI-driven security testing.
